text:
lia: quick heads up — saw a throughput drop on H100 during last night's continuous-batching sweep when per-batch token budget > 512. p95 latency jumped and kernel selection flipped a lot.
ben: ugh, saw that in perf dashboards too. which run id?
lia: run=cb-sweep-20260318-03, pod h100-3. p50 unchanged, p95 from ~42ms -> ~120ms for gen workloads; throughput down ~18%.
amar: curious if it's KV fragmentation causing kernel fallback. any kernel-selector logs?
lia: pasted the relevant bits below:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:45Z] kernel-selector: model=redwood-13b seq=1024 picked=attn_tile_v2 reason=fastpath
[2026-03-18T03:12:46Z] kernel-selector: model=redwood-13b seq=1536 picked=attn_tile_v2 reason=fastpath
[2026-03-18T03:13:02Z] kernel-selector: model=redwood-13b seq=2048 picked=attn_scalar reason=kv_fragmentation>0.3
[2026-03-18T03:13:02Z] runtime: kv_frag=0.34 kv_cache_hits=0.62 pack_ratio=0.71
```
lia: note the kv_fragmentation value spikes right before the slowdown.
rachel: that kv_frag threshold looks like the thing. what's our config for max_tokens_per_batch on H100 for the sweep?
lia: current sweep config (snippet):
```yaml
batching:
  strategy: continuous
  window_ms: 20
  max_tokens_per_batch:
    A10: 1024
    T4: 512
    L4: 768
    A100: 2048
    H100: 1024
  kv_frag_threshold: 0.25
  pack_target: 0.75
```
ben: H100 was 1024 there — that's higher than we usually run in prod. maybe too aggressive for the tiling kernels given our kv fragmentation behavior.
nina: also saw more kernel churn in the trace: tile_v2 -> scalar -> tile_v1 -> scalar. each fallback adds ~8-12ms overhead and fragments caches.
amar: proposal: switch H100 to a sliding-window formation (shorter window_ms + lower max_tokens) so we avoid large seq mixes that force scalar fallback. rough config proposal:
```yaml
batching:
  strategy: sliding_window
  window_ms: 32
  max_tokens_per_batch:
    H100: 384
    A100: 1024
    A10: 768
    L4: 640
    T4: 512
  kv_frag_threshold: 0.2
  pack_target: 0.7
```
amar: rationale: smaller max_tokens reduces chance a single large seq pushes kernel choice to scalar; sliding window lets small requests still join quickly. bump window slightly to let short bursts form stable batches.
lia: can we run a controlled A/B tomorrow? keep production H100 at 512, run this slicing config on a 10% reserved pool and compare p95/p99 and throughput.
ben: +1. also add kernel-hint override for tile_v2 for sequences under 1024 to force stable paths while we measure. e.g. kernel_hint: prefer=attn_tile_v2 for seq<=1024.
rachel: I'll schedule the reservation and the perf job (03:00 UTC). ops-bot, create experiment cb-ab-h100-20260319 with 10% h100 pool.
ops-bot: experiment cb-ab-h100-20260319 created. targets: h100-reserve-10pct. start=2026-03-19T03:00:00Z. alert-cfg=perf-regression.
lia: thanks. follow-ups: 1) run nightly sweep with new config, 2) collect kernel-selector traces + kv_frag histograms, 3) compare p95/p99 and throughput, 4) check pack_ratio and cold-cache behavior.
amar: I'll add a small profiler hook to capture per-batch kv_frag and kernel decisions in the trace so we can correlate.
nina: also add a quick smoke that rejects batches with kv_frag>0.4 (safety) to avoid cascading fallout.
ben: if A/B looks good, we should consider lowering default H100 max to 512 and tune A100 up if stable.
lia: agreed. keeping this thread for notes — I'll dump the perf dashboards and the experiment results here tomorrow. :thumbsup:
